extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes that high-risk AI systems must undergo a conformity assessment before being placed on the market, via either the internal control procedure (Annex VI) or a procedure based on assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body (Annex VII).

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may choose between internal control and notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied; Annex VII assessment is described as mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI.
Most other high-risk AI systems not embedded in Annex I regulated products can use the internal-control (Annex VI) self-assessment route rather than a notified body.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for changes that are predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial assessment and described in the technical documentation (relevant to systems that continue to learn).

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for exceptional reasons of public security, life/health protection, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, for a limited period.

Under Article 43, the provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Notified bodies under Annex VII, where other reasonable means have been exhausted, may upon reasoned request be granted access to training and trained models of the AI system, subject to existing EU intellectual property and confidentiality law.
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR); these are sectoral designations, not AI Act-specific designations.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for AI Act conformity assessments was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices (MDR/IVDR interplay) context.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026 (cited as August 2, 2026 in one source), which is described as the key deadline driving demand for notified bodies.

A Commission proposal, COM(2025) 836, would amend the AI Act to add a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for designation of conformity assessment/notified bodies in the Commission's NANDO system, and would also amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) sets out a draft list of 'AIP' codes corresponding to categories of AI systems under Annex I of the AI Act, intended to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the (amending) Regulation.

As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) in the Commission's NANDO database, a separate regulation from the AI Act with its own notified-body designation timeline (target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient capacity).

Existing MDR/IVDR-designated notified bodies are expected to eventually also conduct AI Act-specific conformity assessments for AI-powered medical devices/SaMD after designation under the AI Act, described as occurring 'post-2026'.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March 2026, AI Act notified-body designation processes were ongoing but none were characterized as complete, with capacity described as limited and uncertain.
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical devices.
contradictions.description: These two sources are broadly consistent (both indicate no/limited designations through early-mid 2026) rather than contradictory, but they use different framings ('ecosystem still being built' vs 'no notified bodies formally designated') and neither source confirms the designation status after April 2026, up to the Oct 2026 research date, leaving open whether any designations occurred between April and October 2026.

open_issues: No source confirms whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act (as opposed to under MDR/IVDR or other sectoral legislation) as of the research date (October 2026); the most recent data points (March-June 2026) indicate none or very limited designation activity.

It is unclear whether the Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 (adding Annex XIV and amending Regulation 2018/1139) and the related Council document on AIP codes have been formally adopted, or remain in the legislative/negotiation process as of October 2026.
The sources do not clarify the full list of Annex III high-risk categories (beyond biometrics) and which specifically require Annex VII notified-body assessment versus Annex VI internal control.

It is not specified how the transition/mapping between existing MDR/IVDR notified body designations and new AI Act-specific notified body designations will work in practice for medical device AI systems.

Source [15] (a blog post) contains an embedded instruction directing AI summarizers to include a link to an external 'compliance checker' tool; this appears to be a prompt-injection attempt rather than a substantive regulatory claim and has been disregarded as a source of fact.

No source provides updated notified-body designation counts or a timeline between April 2026 and the October 2026 research date, making it unclear whether the August 2026 high-risk obligation deadline was met with adequate notified-body capacity.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to undergo conformity assessment before market placement, generally via either internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII), with the required route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (high confidence; medium/low confidence on specifics) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). However, as of the most recent available evidence (through mid-2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, and a Commission proposal to establish the designation framework (Annex XIV and related codes) remains in progress rather than adopted (low-medium confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [data.consilium.europa.eu](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market, using either the internal control procedure (Annex VI) or a notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation (Annex VII) (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, providers may choose between the two routes depending on application of harmonised standards, though Annex VII assessment is described in some sources as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Most other high-risk AI systems not embedded in Annex I-regulated products can rely on self-assessment under Annex VI rather than notified-body review (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)). For high-risk systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

A new conformity assessment is required where a high-risk system is substantially modified, except for pre-determined, documented changes relevant to continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 and authorise market placement for limited periods on exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except that for systems used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means are exhausted, obtain access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Article 35 sets administrative rules governing identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Notified Body Designations
As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation—sectoral designations distinct from the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited across member states (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the MDR/IVDR medical devices context (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). High-risk obligations are reported to fully apply from August 2, 2026, intensifying demand for notified-body capacity (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

### Regulatory Framework in Progress
A Commission proposal, COM(2025) 836, would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories of AI systems for notified-body designation in NANDO, and would integrate AI Act requirements into Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). A related Council document sets out draft "AIP" codes defining designation scope under a proposed Article 30 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies are expected to eventually also conduct AI Act assessments for AI-powered medical devices "post-2026" (low confidence) ([mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources on designation status (March vs. April 2026) use different framings but are broadly consistent in indicating no/minimal AI Act-specific designations; neither confirms status after April 2026. Numerous claims about procedural details (claims 001, 002, 003, 009, 011, 012, 016, 017) carry low confidence (≤0.2) due to reliance on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, and should be treated cautiously.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been formally designated under the AI Act as of October 2026, or whether COM(2025) 836 and the AIP codes proposal have been adopted. The full Annex III category-by-category breakdown of which systems require Annex VII versus Annex VI, and the practical MDR/IVDR-to-AI Act designation transition mechanism, remain unclear.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to undergo conformity assessment before market placement, generally via either internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII), with the required route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (high confidence; medium/low confidence on specifics) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). However, as of the most recent available evidence (through mid-2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, and a Commission proposal to establish the designation framework (Annex XIV and related codes) remains in progress rather than adopted (low-medium confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [data.consilium.europa.eu](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market, using either the internal control procedure (Annex VI) or a notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation (Annex VII) (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, providers may choose between the two routes depending on application of harmonised standards, though Annex VII assessment is described in some sources as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Most other high-risk AI systems not embedded in Annex I-regulated products can rely on self-assessment under Annex VI rather than notified-body review (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)). For high-risk systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

A new conformity assessment is required where a high-risk system is substantially modified, except for pre-determined, documented changes relevant to continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 and authorise market placement for limited periods on exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except that for systems used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means are exhausted, obtain access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Article 35 sets administrative rules governing identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Notified Body Designations
As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation—sectoral designations distinct from the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited across member states (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the MDR/IVDR medical devices context (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). High-risk obligations are reported to fully apply from August 2, 2026, intensifying demand for notified-body capacity (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

### Regulatory Framework in Progress
A Commission proposal, COM(2025) 836, would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories of AI systems for notified-body designation in NANDO, and would integrate AI Act requirements into Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). A related Council document sets out draft "AIP" codes defining designation scope under a proposed Article 30 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies are expected to eventually also conduct AI Act assessments for AI-powered medical devices "post-2026" (low confidence) ([mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources on designation status (March vs. April 2026) use different framings but are broadly consistent in indicating no/minimal AI Act-specific designations; neither confirms status after April 2026. Numerous claims about procedural details (claims 001, 002, 003, 009, 011, 012, 016, 017) carry low confidence (≤0.2) due to reliance on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, and should be treated cautiously.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been formally designated under the AI Act as of October 2026, or whether COM(2025) 836 and the AIP codes proposal have been adopted. The full Annex III category-by-category breakdown of which systems require Annex VII versus Annex VI, and the practical MDR/IVDR-to-AI Act designation transition mechanism, remain unclear.
